record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.original_question: For discrete highest-weight representations D−(j) in string theory on SU(1,1) at level k < −2, is imposing the spin bound k/2 ≤ j < 0 necessary and sufficient to remove all negative-norm physical states after Virasoro constraints, and can this be promoted to a genuine all-level no-ghost theorem?

evidence.quote: The mass-shell condition implies that this representation is present as long as j ≤ −1 (remember k < −2). In that range, unitarity thus demands k/2 ≤ j < 0.
Finally, the question to be answered is still whether the above condition (3.3) can indeed help to restore unitarity.
It is even more puzzling that a real no-ghost theorem might exist, based on the above observations and more specifically on the constraint (3.3) over the spin of the allowed discrete representations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bosonic string theory on the group manifold SU(1,1) ≅ SL(2,ℝ) (covering AdS₃) described by the SL(2,ℝ) WZW model at level k with k < −2. The affine SL(2,ℝ) current algebra admits, among its unitary representations, the discrete lowest-weight representations D⁻(j) labeled by a real spin parameter j, on which the Casimir takes the value −j(j−1) and which contain a primary annihilated by the lowering modes with J₀³ eigenvalue j. Physical string states are obtained by imposing the Virasoro constraints (L_n − δ_{n,0})|phys⟩ = 0 (n ≥ 0) on the tensor product of this current-algebra module with an internal unitary CFT of appropriate central charge so that the total Virasoro central charge equals 26.

Question: For the discrete representations D⁻(j), is the spin restriction
    k/2 ≤ j < 0
both necessary and sufficient to ensure that the space of Virasoro-physical states contains no negative-norm (ghost) states? Equivalently, can one establish a no-ghost theorem, valid at every level k < −2, asserting that under the above spin bound (and its analogue for D⁺(j)) the physical Hilbert space of the SL(2,ℝ) WZW string is positive-definite?
artifact.status_search_result: Maldacena and Ooguri (hep-th/0001053, 2000; J. Math. Phys. 42 (2001) 2929) proved a no-ghost theorem for bosonic string theory on AdS₃/SL(2,ℝ) at all levels k > 2 (in their conventions, equivalently k < −2 in the conventions used here), showing that the spin bound k/2 < j < 0 (together with the analogous bound for D⁺(j) and the inclusion of spectrally flowed sectors) is precisely the condition that yields a ghost-free physical spectrum. Earlier partial results (Evans–Gaberdiel–Perry, Hwang) proved the theorem under the same bound for the unflowed sectors. The problem is therefore considered solved.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 1: The Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: We study the spectrum of bosonic string theory on AdS_3 ... We prove a no-ghost theorem for all the representations that are involved.
status_evidence.claim: Maldacena and Ooguri prove a no-ghost theorem for the SL(2,R) WZW string with the relevant spin bound and spectral flow.

status_evidence.title: The no-ghost theorem for AdS3 and the stringy exclusion principle
status_evidence.snippet: No-ghost theorem for AdS3 ... the restriction on the spin necessary for a ghost-free spectrum corresponds to the stringy exclusion principle.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work (Evans–Gaberdiel–Perry) established the no-ghost theorem under the spin bound j < k/2 for unflowed discrete representations.
